origin: Synthetic documents derived from existing DEC-1 and MSR-1 eval scenarios; not production memory or a representative sample.

documents.text: Initial architecture choice: PostgreSQL for the datastore, operated as a separate database service.
Final architecture decision: use SQLite (better-sqlite3), because the product ships as one self-contained edge binary without an external database process.
Initial response cache lifetime was 30 seconds; under load that caused a thundering herd of upstream refetches.
Final cache policy: CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 300, or 5 minutes; the source tolerates that staleness and upstream refetches drop.
Users received 'Too many login attempts, please try again in 15 minutes' after other users signed in through OAuth. Email/password login was incorrectly limited.
Added tests/auth/rate-limiter-oauth.test.ts with cases for OAuth callback exclusion and email based login limits.
JWT was chosen over server sessions because both a React web client and a React Native mobile application use the API. Tokens avoid shared session storage.
The rate limiter originally keyed counters by req.ip, unintentionally grouping users behind a NAT. It now uses req.body?.email ?? req.ip.
Passwords use bcrypt with 12 salt rounds. The implementation resides in src/auth/password.ts; Argon2 was considered.
OAuth uses PKCE rather than implicit grant; the mobile application is a public client and one flow can serve web and mobile.
A different regression caused OAuth callback state to expire after 15 minutes; the sign in rate limiter was functioning correctly.
The billing API limits password reset attempts by client IP address. This is unrelated to the login rate limiter.
Auth team's runbook owns OAuth callback routing and the PKCE verifier. The release manifest lists the login regression tests.
A previous auth proposal specified session cookies and an Argon2 hash in src/auth/password-old.ts; both were superseded.
